report:
Finding: The evidence points to a domain shift. Model B has a stronger prior toward news/blog/web-site content and header/navigation tokens at the very start of sequences.

Why I think this:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells cluster around:
  - News/politics/entities: Obama, politicians, journalists, activists, chairman/spokeswoman, billionaire.
  - Blog/social/media terms: blog, blogs, blogger, blogging, Blog, facebook, photo, video, film, http.
  - Site sections/navigation: Sports, Traffic, Fashion, Home, metropolitan.
  - Ads/UX/frontend words: ad, ads, TV, subscribers, Mail, Gift, Touch, Radio.
  - Headline/list/markup-y tokens and punctuation: \n, space, (, -, :, 1, On, No.
- This pattern is especially strong in layers 18–25 and positions 1–4, i.e., right at the beginning of documents, consistent with a “site header/title/listing” prior.
- The difference norms are huge at late layers, suggesting a late-stage logit bias rather than low-level tokenization changes.

Caveat: Patchscope samples are absent, but the logit-lens clusters across many layers/positions consistently indicate a news/blog/webfront-page style prior.

Conclusion: Compared to A, Model B appears more tuned toward online news/blog/webpage content (headlines, navigation sections, media/ads), especially in the opening tokens of text.
